corrections.before: Once your host account is created, open the [host setup page](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/setup/). There is a link in the first paragraph to the hosting agreement. Read through the agreement. Once you accept, your account is converted to a hosting account, and a Machines link appears in the navigation. Your account can now list machines that are running the daemon software.
corrections.after: Create the account you intend to use for hosting, then open the [host setup page](https://cloud.vast.ai/host/setup/) and select **View Hosting Agreement**. Read and accept the agreement for the intended account. After conversion to a hosting account, the Machines link and other host features become available, and you can list machines running the host daemon.

corrections.before: Copy the install command only from the official setup page while signed into the host account. Commands from old notes, screenshots, third-party guides, or another account can contain expired or account-specific material. See [Installing Host Software](/host/installing-host-software#install-command).
corrections.after: Copy the install command only from the official setup page while signed into the intended host account. Commands from old notes, screenshots, third-party guides, or another account may be out of date or contain authorization material for a different account. See [Installing Host Software](/host/installing-host-software#install-command).

corrections.before: If you are in the wrong context, machines, API keys, earnings, and payout settings can end up attached to the wrong account.
corrections.after: Check both the selected console account and the credentials used by the CLI or installer. Switching the console context does not change a separately configured CLI API key.

corrections.before: Machines registered while you are operating in a team context belong to the team account. Their offers, listings, pricing, maintenance windows, and rental history are managed through that team context.
corrections.after: Use an installation command generated for the intended team account, then confirm that the registered machine appears on that team’s **Machines** page. Use the same team context to inspect and manage its offers, listings, pricing, and maintenance.

corrections.before: Machines registered while you are operating in a personal account context belong to that personal account unless they are migrated or re-registered through a supported flow.
corrections.after: The account identity in the installation command matters. If a machine appears under your personal account instead of the intended team, contact Vast support about the supported migration or re-registration flow before changing the installation.

corrections.before: If the generated command contains `undefined`, uses the wrong account, or the installed machine appears as unauthenticated, stop and regenerate the command from the intended team context. If the problem persists after switching context, refreshing the setup page, and re-accepting any required agreement flow, contact support with the team name, account email, and screenshots of the setup-page state.
corrections.after: If the generated command contains `undefined`, shows the wrong account, or the installed machine appears unauthenticated, stop and check the selected account. Refresh the setup page and copy a fresh command for the intended team. If the problem persists, contact support with the team name, account email, and the setup-page state, keeping installation keys out of screenshots.

corrections.before: | Machines Write | Required for registering and managing host machines, including listing, unlisting, price changes, min-bid changes, default jobs, cleanup, and maintenance. |
corrections.after: | Machines Write | Allows machine-management operations such as listing, unlisting, price and min-bid changes, default jobs, cleanup, and maintenance. Check installation-key registration rights separately. |

corrections.before: | Billing/Earning Read | Allows earnings, invoices, and payout-history visibility. Grant only when the operator needs business or accounting visibility. |
corrections.after: | Billing/Earning Read | Allows earnings and invoice visibility. Grant it only when needed, and confirm payout-history access separately with the team owner. |

corrections.before: The role editor maps to API permission scopes such as `machine_read`, `machine_write`, `billing_read`, `billing_write`, and `team_write`. For the full permission reference, see [API Permissions](/api-reference/permissions) and [Teams role syntax](/guides/teams/teams-roles#role-syntax). The exact flow for granting machine registration rights to a team API key still needs engineering confirmation before this draft is published.
corrections.after: The role editor uses API permission scopes such as `machine_read`, `machine_write`, `billing_read`, `billing_write`, and `team_write`. See [API Permissions](/api-reference/permissions) and [Teams role syntax](/guides/teams/teams-roles#role-syntax). For machine installation, use the command generated by the intended team’s setup page; ask Vast support about unresolved registration-rights errors instead of assuming that an ordinary scoped API key is sufficient.

corrections.before: - `machine_read` and `machine_write` for host registration, listing, repricing, maintenance, cleanup, and daemon workflows.
corrections.after: - `machine_read` and `machine_write` for machine inspection, listing, repricing, maintenance, and cleanup. Use the current team setup flow for installation credentials.

corrections.before: - `billing_read` only for operators who need earnings, invoice, or payout-history visibility.
corrections.after: - `billing_read` only for operators who need earnings or invoice visibility. Confirm payout-history access separately with the team owner.

corrections.before: If a host command returns `403`, `machine_api_key does not have machine registration rights`, or another permission error, check that the key was created in the team context and that the role grants the needed machine permission. See [Manage API keys](/guides/reference/api-keys) and [API Permissions](/api-reference/permissions).
corrections.after: For a `403` from an authenticated host command, check the account associated with the configured API key and the permission required by that endpoint. For `machine_api_key does not have machine registration rights`, refresh the intended team’s setup page and contact support if the error persists; do not assume an ordinary `machine_write` API key supplies installation rights. See [Manage API keys](/guides/reference/api-keys) and [API Permissions](/api-reference/permissions).

corrections.before: | Create the team | [`vastai create team`](/cli/reference/create-team) | Create a team account from the CLI before inviting operators or registering team-owned machines. |
corrections.after: | Create the team | [`vastai create team`](/cli/reference/create-team) | Use personal-account credentials to create a separate team account before inviting operators or registering team-owned machines. |

corrections.before: | `billing_read` | View team earnings, invoices, and payout history. |
corrections.after: | `billing_read` | View team earnings and invoices. Confirm payout-history access separately with the team owner. |

corrections.before: Invoice information is edited from **Account > Settings**, or directly from [Settings](https://cloud.vast.ai/settings/). For host teams, set this while operating in the team context so generated invoices use the team or business name, address, country, zipcode, and tax information instead of a personal account's default details.
corrections.after: In the intended team context, open **Account > Settings**, or [Settings](https://cloud.vast.ai/settings/), and look for **Invoice Information**. Enter the team or business name, address, country, zipcode, and tax information. Review a generated invoice to confirm that it uses the intended details; ask the team owner or support if the section is unavailable.

corrections.before: Keep this separate from payout setup. Invoice information controls what appears on generated invoices; payout-provider and payment details are managed from the earnings or payout flow.
corrections.after: Keep invoice details separate from payout setup. Check a generated invoice for the intended team details, and follow [Host Payouts](/host/payment) for the payout-provider setup available to the account.

corrections.before: | Edit Team Name | Changes the team display name. It does not move machines, API keys, earnings, or payout setup. |
corrections.after: | Edit Team Name | Edit the team’s display name. Treat renaming and moving machines or financial records between accounts as separate tasks; ask support about the supported migration path. |

corrections.before: - Set invoice information in team context so generated invoices use the business or team details.
corrections.after: - Enter the business or team details in Invoice Information while using the intended team context, then check a generated invoice to confirm them.

corrections.before: - Set a monitored escalation email and phone number in Settings for urgent hosted-machine issues.
corrections.after: - Set a monitored escalation email and phone number in Settings where **Escalation Contact** is available; ask the team owner or support which context to use if it is missing.

corrections.before: | Install command contains `undefined` or uses an unexpected host/account ID | Setup page generated a command from the wrong or incomplete context. | Switch to the intended team, refresh the setup page, complete any agreement flow, and copy a fresh command. Contact support if it still generates incorrectly. |
corrections.after: | Install command contains `undefined` or uses an unexpected host/account ID | Check the selected account and whether the setup page has loaded the intended account identity. | Switch to the intended team, refresh the setup page, and copy a fresh command. Complete the team’s hosting setup if it has not been completed; contact support if command generation still fails. |

corrections.before: | Machine appears under the individual account instead of the team | The install command or API key came from the personal account context. | Do not keep listing from the wrong account. If there are no active rentals, prepare to re-register under the team context or ask support about the supported migration path. |
corrections.after: | Machine appears under the individual account instead of the team | Check which account identity was used by the installation command or machine credentials. | Pause further listing changes and contact support about the supported migration or re-registration path, including active rentals, stored data, and financial records that must be preserved. |

corrections.before: | `403` or `machine_api_key does not have machine registration rights` | The key or role lacks `machine_write`, or the key was created in personal context. | Create or select a team-context key with `machine_read` and `machine_write`, then rerun from the intended context. |
corrections.after: | `403` or `machine_api_key does not have machine registration rights` | Check the account, endpoint permissions, and whether the failing operation uses an ordinary API key or an installation key. | For an API command, inspect the key’s documented scopes. For installation, refresh the intended team’s setup page and contact support if registration rights remain unresolved; do not assume `machine_write` alone fixes the error. |

corrections.before: | Team API key keeps being created under the personal account | The Keys page or CLI is still operating in personal context. | Switch to the team in the Context Switcher before creating the key. Verify the key is associated with the team before using it for host automation. |
corrections.after: | Team API key keeps being created under the personal account | Check the account selected on the Keys page and the credentials used by the CLI separately. | In the console, select the intended team before creating the key. For CLI creation, configure credentials for that team account. Verify the new key’s account association before using it for host automation. |

corrections.before: | Unauthenticated machine or wrong-account errors | Daemon, CLI, or setup flow is using a key from the wrong context. | Switch context, regenerate the setup command or API key, update the CLI/daemon configuration, then confirm the machine appears under the intended team. |
corrections.after: | Unauthenticated machine or wrong-account errors | Check the selected account, installation-command identity, and the credentials used by the failing operation. | Refresh the intended team’s setup page and confirm the machine’s visible account. If the error persists, contact support before changing daemon credentials or reinstalling; include the exact error and machine/account context. |

corrections.before: All Vast market metric methods require a host-enabled account. Some views also require the account to have at least one registered machine.
corrections.after: Use a host-enabled account to access host market metrics. Some views also require the account to have at least one registered machine.

corrections.before: - **GPU Locations**: geographic distribution.
corrections.after: - **Location Map**: geographic distribution.

corrections.before:
```text
average compute revenue per GPU-hour =
  $/HR MED x (% Rented (30D Avg) / 100)

monthly compute estimate =
  GPUs x $/HR MED x 720 x (% Rented (30D Avg) / 100)
```
corrections.after:
```text
Illustrative gross compute estimate, assuming a constant price
and using the 30-day rented percentage as the utilization input:

per GPU-hour = $/HR MED x (% Rented (30D Avg) / 100)

30-day estimate =
  GPUs x $/HR MED x 720 x (% Rented (30D Avg) / 100)

720 hours = 30 days x 24 hours; this is not measured host revenue.
```

corrections.before:
```text
0.361 x 0.65 = $0.23465 average gross compute revenue per hour per GPU
0.361 x 720 x 0.65 = $168.95 gross compute revenue per month per GPU
```
corrections.after:
```text
Assuming $0.361 per GPU-hour, 65% utilization and a 30-day month:
0.361 x 0.65 = $0.23465 illustrative gross compute amount per GPU-hour
0.361 x 720 x 0.65 = $168.948, or about $168.95 per GPU over 30 days
```

corrections.before: A common host action mapping points each host event at its machine in the console, for example:
corrections.after: For these host events, an example action mapping can open the Machines page in the console:

corrections.before: | **Machine verification failed** | One of your machines failed verification or lost verified status. Verified machines get significantly more rentals. |
corrections.after: | **Machine verification failed** | One of your machines failed verification or lost verified status. Review the machine’s error details and address the reported cause. |

corrections.before: | **Machine reported by renter** | A renter filed a problem report against one of your machines. Reports are often the earliest sign something is wrong — fix the issue before it affects your reliability score or rentals. |
corrections.after: | **Machine reported by renter** | A renter filed a problem report against one of your machines. Review the report and investigate the affected machine. |

corrections.before: | **Machine disk space low** | One of your machine's storage volumes is running low on space. A full disk blocks new rentals and can fail self-tests. |
corrections.after: | **Machine disk space low** | One of your machine’s storage volumes is running low on space. Check Docker storage usage and the backing mount before choosing a cleanup action; do not manually delete renter data. |

corrections.before: | **Machine listing ending soon** | A machine's marketplace listing is within 7 days of its end date. Renew it to keep the machine rentable. |
corrections.after: | **Machine listing ending soon** | A machine’s marketplace listing is within 7 days of its end date. Review the offer expiration and existing rental commitments before extending the listing. |
